question: After the integration blockers and exact-head device proof are addressed, does the bounded phone-proxy-only Data Layer design meet the intended v1 security and release boundary?
rationale: The feature exposes sessions, transcript content, send, and abort operations across devices and changes signed Play release handling; the protected maintainer signal and canonical issue explicitly require human product/security approval.

options.title: Approve phone-proxy v1
options.body: Keep the five-method allowlist and phone-owned credentials, require the identified gate fixes and exact-head physical proof, then land the consolidated companion.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Limit v1 to status or read-only transcript behavior and defer send, abort, voice, TTS, and notifications to later reviewed changes.

options.title: Pause first-party Wear
options.body: Do not ship the companion until maintainers are ready to own the additional Android security, Play release, and device-proof surface.

recommendation.title: Approve phone-proxy v1
recommendation.body: Keep the five-method allowlist and phone-owned credentials, require the identified gate fixes and exact-head physical proof, then land the consolidated companion.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the canonical product direction and current Wear protocol path and are best positioned to confirm the intended boundary.
